title: Family Conflict Psychoeducation: Three-Level Learning Pathway
description: Canonical SafeSteps family conflict psychoeducation program configuration with three-level progression and reusable assessments.

content.overview: Canonical three-level family conflict psychoeducation pathway for child-safe, privacy-respecting educational practice.

program.title: Family Conflict Psychoeducation: Three-Level Learning Pathway
program.audience: Parents and children, taught together when appropriate or separately when privacy or safety requires it
safeguards: Keep children out of adult disputes; do not ask them to carry messages, report on a parent, or choose sides.
Use fictional scenarios for practice. Participants may pass, take a break, or choose another way to participate.
Respect privacy. Follow applicable safeguarding procedures if safety concerns arise.
This program is educational and is not a substitute for therapy, legal advice, or professional assessment.
Mastery means demonstrated learning, not perfection or a judgment about someone's parenting.

lessons.title: Understanding Family Conflict
lessons.learning_goal: Recognize common forms of conflict and distinguish adult responsibilities from children's responsibilities.

Basic.activity: Sort examples into adult problems and child responsibilities.

Developing.activity: Analyze a fictional family scenario and identify how conflict may affect a child.

Mastery.activity: Create a family-specific plan for keeping children out of conflict.

lessons.title: Loyalty Conflicts
lessons.learning_goal: Recognize loyalty pressure and affirm that children do not need to choose sides.

Basic.activity: Identify feelings a child might have when asked to take sides.

Developing.activity: Role-play reassuring a child that they do not need to choose sides.

Mastery.activity: Analyze a complex fictional scenario involving pressure from multiple adults and plan a child-centered response.

lessons.title: Effects on Well-Being
lessons.learning_goal: Identify possible signs of stress without diagnosing, and consider supportive next steps.

Basic.activity: Match possible stress signals with supportive responses.

Developing.activity: Review a fictional case and distinguish observations from assumptions.

Mastery.activity: Develop a proportionate support plan, including when to seek professional help.

lessons.title: Listening and Validation
lessons.learning_goal: Practice listening, reflecting feelings, and responding without blame or pressure.

Basic.activity: Practice reflecting a feeling in one sentence.

Developing.activity: Use listening skills in a paired conversation with a neutral prompt.

Mastery.activity: Demonstrate listening in a challenging simulated conversation while respecting a person's choice not to share.

lessons.title: Calm Communication
lessons.learning_goal: Use respectful, specific language to express feelings and needs.

Basic.activity: Complete an 'I feel... when... I would like...' sentence.

Developing.activity: Rewrite blaming statements and practice a calm request.

Mastery.activity: Use clear, respectful communication in a scenario with disagreement and competing needs.

lessons.title: Emotional Regulation
lessons.learning_goal: Recognize escalation cues and choose a safe pause or coping strategy.

Basic.activity: Name two signs of escalation and two coping strategies.

Developing.activity: Sequence a pause-and-return plan for a fictional disagreement.

Mastery.activity: Demonstrate choosing and adapting a regulation strategy during a simulated difficult interaction.

lessons.title: Children Are Not Messengers
lessons.learning_goal: Identify inappropriate roles for children and practice adult-owned communication.

Basic.activity: Identify which messages belong between adults.

Developing.activity: Practice redirecting a child who has been asked to carry a message.

Mastery.activity: Create and evaluate a practical communication-boundary plan for recurring situations.

lessons.title: Speaking Respectfully About the Other Parent
lessons.learning_goal: Avoid putting children in the middle while communicating honestly and appropriately.

Basic.activity: Choose a neutral, reassuring response from several options.

Developing.activity: Rewrite critical comments into age-appropriate, child-focused language.

Mastery.activity: Respond to a child's difficult question while being honest, respectful, and appropriately boundaried.

lessons.title: Transitions and Schedule Changes
lessons.learning_goal: Reduce uncertainty around transitions and create practical plans for changes.

Basic.activity: Follow a simple transition checklist.

Developing.activity: Plan for a fictional delay or schedule change.

Mastery.activity: Build a workable transition plan with a backup option and child-friendly explanation.

lessons.title: Repair After Conflict
lessons.learning_goal: Recognize when repair is needed and practice an accountable apology.

Basic.activity: Identify the parts of a sincere apology.

Developing.activity: Practice acknowledging impact and naming a realistic change.

Mastery.activity: Demonstrate repair without excuses, pressure, or asking a child to comfort the adult.

lessons.title: Expressing Feelings Safely
lessons.learning_goal: Offer developmentally appropriate ways to express feelings while respecting a choice not to share.

Basic.activity: Choose from several safe ways to express a feeling.

Developing.activity: Practice responding supportively when someone shares or declines to share a feeling.

Mastery.activity: Create a personalized, voluntary expression-and-support plan.
assessment: Journal or plan review, with privacy respected

lessons.title: Coping and Support Networks
lessons.learning_goal: Build a menu of coping strategies and identify trusted support people.

Basic.activity: Match a common feeling to a possible coping strategy.

Developing.activity: Create a support map and practice asking a trusted person for help.

Mastery.activity: Compare coping options for different situations and explain when additional support may be needed.

lessons.title: Co-Parenting Communication
lessons.learning_goal: Communicate about practical child needs with brief, neutral, respectful messages.

Basic.activity: Identify clear and respectful features in a sample message.

Developing.activity: Draft a brief message about a fictional child-related issue.

Mastery.activity: Edit a complex message for clarity, relevance, tone, boundaries, and agreed communication channels.

lessons.title: Problem-Solving Under Constraints
lessons.learning_goal: Create workable, child-centered plans that account for real-life constraints.

Basic.activity: Identify the problem and one practical option in a simple scenario.

Developing.activity: Plan around a fictional time, transport, or schedule constraint.

Mastery.activity: Compare options, anticipate obstacles, and create a realistic backup plan.

lessons.title: Digital Communication and Privacy
lessons.learning_goal: Use digital communication responsibly and protect children from adult conflict online.

Basic.activity: Identify basic privacy and messaging do's and don'ts.

Developing.activity: Rewrite an emotionally charged text as a neutral practical message.

Mastery.activity: Develop a digital communication plan addressing privacy, timing, boundaries, and child involvement.

lessons.title: Escalation and Safe Next Steps
lessons.learning_goal: Notice when a conversation is becoming unproductive and choose a safe next step.

Basic.activity: Recognize signs that a conversation should pause.

Developing.activity: Use a decision tree to choose whether to continue, pause, or seek support.

Mastery.activity: Respond to an ambiguous scenario, explain the reasoning, and identify when safeguarding or professional procedures apply.

lessons.title: Developmental Needs
lessons.learning_goal: Adjust explanations and expectations to a child's age and developmental abilities.

Basic.activity: Match a simple explanation to a child's age or developmental level.

Developing.activity: Adapt the same explanation for different age groups.

Mastery.activity: Explain a difficult topic in an age-appropriate way and check understanding without pressure.

lessons.title: Predictability and Emotional Safety
lessons.learning_goal: Create routines and agreements that help children know what to expect.

Basic.activity: Identify routines that can help children know what to expect.

Developing.activity: Map a fictional week and mark transitions or uncertainties.

Mastery.activity: Create and review a realistic routine plan, including how adults will explain changes.

lessons.title: Reviewing Progress
lessons.learning_goal: Track changes over time and identify when support may need adjustment.

Basic.activity: Complete a confidence rating and name one skill to practice.

Developing.activity: Review several weeks of reflections and identify a learning trend.

Mastery.activity: Use evidence over time to adjust goals or support without blame or unsupported conclusions.

lessons.title: Integration and Next Steps
lessons.learning_goal: Apply key skills to a realistic scenario and identify ongoing supports.

Basic.activity: Recall key ideas and choose one skill to practice.

Developing.activity: Work through an integrated fictional case with several decision points.

Mastery.activity: Demonstrate integrated skills, explain reasoning, and create a realistic continuing-learning plan.

Basic.description: Recognize and explain key ideas, feelings, boundaries, and basic strategies.

Developing.description: Apply skills in fictional scenarios and create practical plans with support.

Mastery.description: Integrate and adapt skills in complex situations, explain reasoning, and show growth over time.

completion_guidance.progression: Learners may progress at different rates. Use a brief pre-check to select a starting level, provide review when needed, and allow learners to demonstrate understanding in more than one way.

exit_ticket: One thing I'm still unsure about:

criteria: Keeps children out of adult conflict

learning_journal_prompts: What was the biggest challenge you faced today?
What would you do differently next time?
What question would you like to ask a trusted adult or facilitator?
What is one example of progress you noticed this week?
